It is recommended that no matter SEO novices or veterans, read it slowly!</p>

<h2 id="toc-1">GTM big update: Server-Side Tagging</h2>
<p>Google Tag Manager has launched server-side tagging. It is currently only open to the Google Cloud Platform environment, but it is believed to be integrated with more environments.</p>
<p>This is very different from the general GTM. I have read the introduction several times and still am confused. I can only roughly understand the advantages of server side tagging. Here is a very brief introduction. Interested readers can do their own research and welcome to discuss with me! If anyone finds good Chinese resources, please let me know. I will be happy to share them in the digital engine so that more people can see~</p>
<figure class="embed embed--youtube"><div class="embed__frame"><iframe allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen="" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/6OGbOh216mU" title="YouTube video player"></iframe></div><figcaption><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6OGbOh216mU" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original video on YouTube</a></figcaption></figure>
<p><strong>In general settings (client-side)</strong>, third-party javascript will be loaded on the web page, which will consume browser resources, may make the web page load slower, and webmasters have no control over what data is sent to the third party.<strong>via server-side tagging</strong>, GTM uses HTTP Requests to understand what is happening on the web page, and leaves it to the "Client" for processing. After the processing is completed, it decides what data to send to the third party (ex: intercepted<code>/r/collect?v=1&amp;..</code>will send a pageview to Google Analytics).</p>
<p>In other words, third parties (such as Facebook) will not be able to track various things just because they ask the website administrator to install a pixel through client-side GTM. Instead, they can only receive the data that you define on the server-side GTM to be transmitted to the third party. It has the advantages of privacy, performance, data accuracy, etc., but the disadvantage is complexity and additional costs.</p>
<p>link:<a href="https://developers.google.com/tag-manager/serverside">official article</a> / <a href="https://www.simoahava.com/analytics/server-side-tagging-google-tag-manager/">Simo article</a></p>
<hr class="wp-block-separator"/>
</div></div>

<h2 id="toc-2">Create your People Card on Google</h2>

<h2 id="toc-3">Official article: How quality raters make search results better</h2>
<p>Posted by Danny Sullivan<a href="https://blog.google/products/search/raters-experiments-improve-google-search/">Article</a>is talking about how Google uses some insights to optimize search results and rankings.</p>
<p>A large part of the article talks about the concept of Quality Raters. Basically, Google employs more than 10,000 people around the world to rate the quality of search results. They base<a href="https://static.googleusercontent.com/media/guidelines.raterhub.com/en//searchqualityevaluatorguidelines.pdf">A guide (search quality guidelines)
The criteria on</a>are used to score search engine results, including whether the web page meets the search intent, whether it has EAT... and so on. Their decision does not directly affect the ranking of the website, but is used to measure whether Google search has achieved the goal of meeting user needs.</p>
<p>If you have never heard of search quality raters or are unfamiliar with this concept, it is recommended to read this article!</p>

<h2 id="toc-5">8/11 Big glitch in Google index</h2>
<p>On the afternoon of 8/11 US time, many people noticed a considerable change in the rankings of the search results, thinking that Google had launched an algorithm update. However, officials later clarified that it was a chain reaction caused by a problem in a certain link in the indexing system.</p>
<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img alt="Google traffic changes on August 10th" class="wp-image-1618" decoding="async" height="170" loading="lazy" src="./wp-content/uploads/2020/08/google-08-10-%E6%B5%81%E9%87%8F%E7%95%B0%E5%8B%95.jpg" width="800"/><figcaption><a href="https://courses.mariehaynes.com/search-news-you-can-use/episode-145-light-version/?ck_subscriber_id=207851014#ftoc-heading-7:~:text=Monday%20this%20week%20was%20quite%20interesting">Websites affected by this bug</a></figcaption></figure>
<blockquote class="embed embed--twitter"><p>Twitter／X Post</p><a href="https://twitter.com/JohnMu/status/1293045032124059649" rel="noopener noreferrer">View original post on Twitter／X</a></blockquote>
<p>The way Google operates is roughly divided into<a href="./how-search-engines-crawl.html">grab</a>", "Index" and "Ranking", the three stages are closely linked. This time everyone thought that the ranking algorithm had been changed, but it was later confirmed that there was a problem in the indexing stage.<a href="./seo-newsletter-issue-12.html#toc-11">few weeks</a>Gary also mentioned another problem in a podcast that seemed to be an index problem, but was actually an indirect result caused by a problem with a program in the crawling process.</p>
<p>link:<a href="https://www.seroundtable.com/google-indexing-system-failure-29934.html">SER report</a> / <a href="https://twitter.com/methode/status/1293229288527994887">Gary explanation retrieval system (Caffeine)</a></p>

<p>In order to promote communication between webmasters and SEOs, Google held this online discussion. Each session will have a theme and the host will lead the discussion. <h2 id="toc-9">SEO Mythbusters: Canonicalization</h2>
<p>The myth buster in this episode is about Canonicalization (consolidation of duplicate URLs). I think the topic is well chosen.
The main axis of<strong>canonicalization is how search engines determine whether the content on different web pages is the same or different.</strong>. It sounds simple, but in practice it is not, for example<em>If the content may have only slight differences, is it considered duplicate content? How to integrate the same content appearing on different web pages at the same time?</em>...etc. Points discussed in this episode include:</p>
<ul><li>canonical tag in the process of canonicalization<strong>is just one of the signals</strong>, not a command, Google has other signals used to determine</li><li>What happens when the content is inconsistent but there is canonical, or the content is consistent but there is no canonical?</li><li>canonical vs redirect</li><li>Website canonical preference vs user preference?</li></ul>
